address.note: Google Maps geocodes the bare street address '8181 NW 36th St, Doral, FL' to postal code 33178 (a building-only pin with no business attached, see google_maps_check below), one digit off from the 33166 every business directory lists. phone_source: Task brief (already verified) plus independently corroborated live via Birdeye profile page, Yelp search snippet, Angi profile ('About us' + listing header), and LinkedIn company page (matches exactly, LinkedIn also lists a fax number 305-428-8485).

email_confidence: low-medium: found on the company's own LinkedIn company page as its listed contact email, but the domain miamicleaningservice.net does NOT resolve (curl: 'Could not resolve host', confirmed twice). Recorded per pipeline rule (real, sourced, not invented) but NOT used as the primary outreach channel; phone is used as primary contact instead. email_search_log.method: Fetched full page twice with WebFetch (once for general info, once specifically asking for verbatim reviews/photos/email/social), and once more directly with Playwright (see photo research below) to read all and body text.
email_search_log.result: No email found. Page shows 'Profile Status: Unclaimed by business owner'; no mailto link, no About section with contact details beyond phone/address/hours.

email_search_log.method: Fetched with WebFetch and separately with curl + Chrome UA (200 OK, 109KB HTML saved and grepped).
email_search_log.result: FOUND: info@miamicleaningservice.net, listed as the company's official contact email in LinkedIn's company-info panel, alongside fax 305-428-8485 and a website field pointing to http://www.miamicleaningservice.net/ (a domain that no longer resolves, see below).

email_search_log.source: miamicleaningservice.net (the domain LinkedIn lists as the company website, and the domain of the email LinkedIn lists)
email_search_log.method: curl direct fetch of both http://miamicleaningservice.net/ and http://www.miamicleaningservice.net/.
email_search_log.result: DNS resolution failure on both ('Could not resolve host'). The domain is not currently registered/resolving at all, so this domain (and by extension the info@miamicleaningservice.net address) is almost certainly dead today, even though it was real enough for the business to list on LinkedIn at some point.

email_search_log.source: miamicleaningservice.com (the domain given in the task brief)
email_search_log.method: curl direct fetch with Chrome UA of http://www.miamicleaningservice.com/, then followed its client-side JS redirect to /lander.
email_search_log.result: Root resolves (HTTP 200) but returns a 114-byte page whose only content is a script tag that does 'window.location.href="/lander"'; no real page content. Following that redirect to /lander returns HTTP 503 with the literal body text 'DNS resolution failure'. So the .com domain is registered and technically 'up' but serves nothing but a broken parking-service redirect loop; no contact info, no mailto, nothing extractable. See website_check for the full has_own_site determination.

email_search_log.source: Facebook (facebook.com/mcs.commercial and facebook.com/cleanandcleaners, the two candidates from the task brief)
email_search_log.method: Attempted WebFetch and curl+Chrome-UA on both URLs directly (both blocked by Facebook's unauthenticated login wall, HTTP 400/login page with zero business data extractable); then ran a targeted 'site:facebook.com' web search for each handle to read the indexed snippet instead.
email_search_log.result: cleanandcleaners: search snippet reveals this is a DIFFERENT company, 'Clean and Cleaners', phone (305) 699-9588, email service@cleanandcleaners.com, which does NOT match our target's phone (305) 428-8484. Confirmed NOT this business; dropped entirely, not used anywhere on the site or registry. mcs.commercial: search snippet describes a Miami commercial-cleaning page (offices/Airbnbs) with no address or phone visible in the snippet, so it could not be positively matched to this residential Doral business either; also dropped as unconfirmed (no email surfaced from it regardless).

email_search_log.method: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 directly; retried successfully via a local Playwright browser (see photo research for the TLS-fix method) which rendered the full page and its body text.
email_search_log.result: No email found. 'About us' section only gives a one-line bio and business highlights (family owned, 21 years of experience, emergency services offered); Angi routes contact through its own lead-request system, not a published email.

email_search_log.method: Attempted WebFetch (HTTP 403), curl with Chrome UA (returned Yelp's DataDome bot-challenge page, not real content), and 3 separate Playwright attempts (TLS-fix launch args, then with 12s wait, then with simulated mouse movement/scrolling over ~17s) to get past the challenge.
email_search_log.result: Never got past the DataDome 'Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker' challenge page in any attempt; page title stayed 'yelp.com' and body text stayed empty every time. No email (or any other content) recoverable from Yelp.

email_search_log.method: Web search for the business name plus 'Instagram'.
email_search_log.result: No account found; the search surfaced unrelated Doral-area cleaning businesses (Miami Bin Cleaner, Well Clean Services) but nothing for Miami Cleaning Service Inc itself.

email_search_log.method: 6 different Playwright-driven Google Maps searches (business name alone, business name + address, business name + city/state, exact address, exact address + zip, and the phone number by itself).
email_search_log.result: The business never appeared in any result list, despite dozens of other Doral/Miami cleaning competitors surfacing for the same queries. No Google Business Profile page (and therefore no email, hours, or photos) could be located this way; see photos.source_attempts for the full detail and the working theory (listing gone dormant/delisted since review activity stopped around 2016-2017).

domains_tested.result: Resolves (HTTP 200) but the root page is a 114-byte stub containing only a JS redirect to /lander; /lander itself returns HTTP 503 with body text 'DNS resolution failure'. No usable content, no menu, no contact form, nothing. This matches the task brief's own re-check (blank page via WebFetch) plus this session's own curl re-check, which additionally surfaced the broken /lander redirect loop underneath the blank appearance.

Does not resolve at all (DNS failure). This is the domain LinkedIn's company page currently lists as the business's website and the domain of its listed email; it appears to have expired/lapsed since LinkedIn last synced that field.

website_check.conclusion: has_own_site = false. Neither domain associated with this business currently serves a real, working site. miamicleaningservice.com is the stronger outreach hook of the two ('your website isn't loading') because it is still registered and technically resolves, it just serves a broken parking-service redirect to nowhere; per FORGE-BRIEF 0.b this is treated as NOT a functioning website, same as the rapalo-landscaping-north-miami and otechlandscaping precedents for broken/placeholder domains.

instagram_note: No verifiable Instagram account found after web search (see email_search_log). Not used anywhere.
facebook_note: Two candidate Facebook pages from the task brief were checked (facebook.com/mcs.commercial and facebook.com/cleanandcleaners). cleanandcleaners is confirmed to be a DIFFERENT business (different phone, different email domain). mcs.commercial could not be positively matched to this specific Doral residential business (no address/phone visible in any accessible snippet, and the page itself is blocked by Facebook's login wall for both WebFetch and curl). photos.conclusion: 0 of the required 5 real, verified, business-specific photos were found. This is a hard research dead end given the tools available in this environment (Yelp's DataDome bot-wall and Google's own captcha-wall both actively defeated repeated, varied automated attempts; Google Maps' own listing for the business appears to no longer be indexed/discoverable at all; every other channel checked (Birdeye, LinkedIn, Angi) explicitly confirms it holds only placeholder/stock imagery, not zero-effort gaps).

research_degradado_note: This is NOT a case of degraded/automated research per FORGE-BRIEF 0.b's rescate clause: no automated photo-fetch service was used and silently returned too little. Every source was checked by hand with a real rendered browser (Playwright, TLS-fixed per the documented sandbox workaround) or direct fetch, multiple times, with several distinct techniques per source.
